# Part 1: More Advanced Data Types
---
# Common Data Types in R

.pull-left[
- Numeric
  * integer: 1, 2, 3
  * double: 1.12124

- Character (aka string)
  * "hello"

- Logical
  * T/F (TRUE/FALSE)
]

.pull-right[
- Vectors and lists
  * Two different ways to store and manipulate data

- Datetime
  * "2026-10-18"

- Factor
  * eye_colors <- c("Blue", "Green", "Brown")
  * factor(eye_colors)
]

---
# What Packages Do We Need?

- Default tidyverse
  * `ggplot2`: Graphing
  * `tibble`: Using tibble-style dataframes
  * `tidyr`: Shaping tibbles and columns
  * `purrr`: Automating/iterating (instead of loops)
  * `dplyr`: Selecting, filtering, and transforming dataframes
  * `stringr`: Manipulating strings
  * `forcats`: Manipulating factors
  * `lubridate`: Manipulating dates

---
# Character Data (Strings)

- At minimum, working with characters is needed to deal with file paths

- String functions let you clean up messy text input

- Understanding how to construct and format strings can help you avoid hard-coding things like graph labels and output tables

- Learning how to wrangle strings and exploit patterns helps write more efficient code (e.g., selecting and mutating columns with `contains()`, `starts_with()`, etc.)

- The `stringr` package has a suite of helper functions for common string operations

```{r, include = F}
ds <- read_csv('data_cleaned/vocab_annoying_headers.csv') %>% 
  mutate(id = "Jonah", dob = as.Date("2017-08-30"), .before = "age_12")
ds <- ds %>% pivot_longer(-(id:dob), names_to = "age", values_to = "word", values_drop_na = T, names_prefix = "age_") %>%
  select(-id, -dob)
```
---
# stringr Cheatsheet

.content-box-blue[
`r icons::fontawesome("github")` [View on RStudio GitHub](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/html/strings.html)
]

---
# Jonah's first words
```{r}
ds$word
```

---
# Length, Detecting Strings, & Counting Strings
```{r}
ds %>% mutate(word_length = str_length(word), 
              has_b = str_detect(word, "b"), 
              num_b = str_count(word, "b"))
```

---
# Regular Expressions (regex)

- A **pattern language** for matching text, used in `stringr` functions like `str_detect()`, `str_extract()`, `str_replace_all()`
- In R strings, a backslash must be doubled: `"\\d"`, `"\\."`
.pull-left[
.bold[Characters and classes]
- `.` any character
- `\\d` digit, `\\w` word character, `\\s` space
- `[aeiou]` any one of these
- `[^aeiou]` anything but these
- `[:alpha:]`, `[:digit:]`, `[:punct:]` anything in this class
]
.pull-right[
.bold[Anchors]
- `^` start of string
- `$` end of string
- `\\b` word boundary
]

---
# Regular Expressions (regex)

.pull-left[
.bold[Quantifiers]
- `?` 0 or 1
- `*` 0 or more
- `+` 1 or more
- `{3}` exactly 3, `{2,4}` 2 to 4
]
.pull-right[
.bold[Alternatives and groups]
- `a|b` a or b
- `(ab)+` group, then repeat
- `\\.` a literal period (escape special characters)
]
.content-box-blue[
`r icons::fontawesome("github")` [RStudio regex cheatsheet](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/regex.pdf)
]
---
`r chunk_reveal("patterns", break_type = "rotate", float = "none", widths = c(12, 1), title = "# Matching Patterns")`

```{r patterns, include = F}
ds %>% mutate(contains_punct = str_detect(word, "[:punct:]")) #ROTATE
ds %>% mutate(word_cleaned = str_remove_all(word, "[:punct:]")) #ROTATE
ds %>% mutate(word_cleaned = str_replace_all(word, "[:punct:]"," ")) #ROTATE
ds %>% mutate(vowel_count = str_count(word, "[aeiou]")) #ROTATE

```

```{r}
fnames <- list.files(path="data_raw", full.names = T)
print(fnames)
```

---

`r chunk_reveal("morepatterns", break_type = "rotate", float = "none", widths = c(12, 1), title = "# Matching Patterns")`

```{r morepatterns, include = F}
fnames <- list.files(path="data_raw", full.names = T)
str_split(fnames, "/") #ROTATE
str_replace_all(fnames, "data_raw/|.csv|vocab","") #ROTATE
str_extract_all(fnames, "\\d{2}.\\d{1}|\\d{2}", simplify = T) #ROTATE
str_extract_all(fnames, "\\.[:alpha:]{1,4}", simplify = T) #ROTATE
str_extract_all(ds$word, boundary("word"), simplify = T) #ROTATE

```

---
`r chunk_reveal("combiningstrings", break_type = "rotate", float = "none", widths = c(12, 1), title = "# Combining Strings")`
```{r combiningstrings, include = F}
age <- seq(from = 12, to = 24, by = .5) 
paste0("data_raw/vocab", age, ".csv") #ROTATE
str_glue("data_raw/vocab{age}.csv") #ROTATE

```
---
# Logical (T/F)

- Logical data are usually created by comparisons or tests in R rather than data we collected
  * Created by operators like `>`,`<`,`==`,`!=`,`>=`, `%in%`, `is.na()`, `str_detect()`, etc.
  * Also inside mutate(), filter(), etc.

- FALSE = 0, TRUE = 1
  * sum() counts matches and mean() gives a proportion of TRUEs

---

`r chunk_reveal("logicals", break_type = "auto", widths = c(1, 0), display_type = "code", title = "# Logicals from Text")`

```{r logicals, include = FALSE}
contains_b <- str_detect(ds$word, "b") # TRUE if the word contains b
contains_b 
typeof(contains_b) 
sum(contains_b) 
mean(contains_b) 
!contains_b 
ds$word[contains_b] 
ds %>% mutate(contains_b = contains_b) 
ds %>% filter(contains_b) 
ds %>% mutate(b_and_vowels = contains_b & str_detect(word, "[aeiou]"))
ds <- ds %>% mutate(b_or_startswithd = contains_b | str_starts(word, "d"))  
```
---
# Vectors and Lists: Collections of Values

- Vectors are type-homogeneous

  * Numeric vectors, `c(1,2,3,4,5)`, `1:5`
  * Character vectors,  `c("Hello", "Goodbye")`
  * Logical vectors, `c(T, T, T, F, T, F)`
  * Vector items can be named `c(x = 1, y = 2)`

- Lists are type-heterogeneous

  * Mix types, `list("1", 1, TRUE, 1:5)`
  * Tibbles are lists of vectors/lists of the same length

---
`r chunk_reveal("vectors", break_type = "auto", widths = c(2, 1), title = "# Vectors")`

```{r vectors, include = FALSE}
v <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
v
typeof(v)
length(v)
v[1] # Use brackets to access a vector element
v[3]
v <- c(v, 6, 7, 8) # use c to add items
v <- c(1, 2, 3, "4", "5", "6") 
v # You cannot mix types in a vector
v <- c(x = 1, y = 2, z = 3) # Named vector
v
v['y']

files <- list.files(path = "data_raw")
files[1] # Character vector
files[2]
length(files) 
```

---
`r chunk_reveal("lists", break_type = "auto", widths = c(2, 1), title = "# Lists")`

```{r lists, include = FALSE}
lt <- list(x = 1, y = "3", z = 1:5)
lt
lt$z # Access named list elements with $
lt[[1]] # Use double brackets to get list elements
lt[[3]] <- 5:7

# List of lists
lt <- list(lt1 = lt, lt2 = lt, lt3 = lt)
lt$lt1

model <- lm(height ~ mass, data = starwars)
typeof(model)
model$coefficients
```

# Working with Dates and Times
- Correctly parse dates/times from character data

- Calculate differences between dates/times (e.g., ages, task length)

- Determine local time using time zones


```{r, include = F}
dates <- tibble(dates1 = c("2017-09-01", "2016-09-01", "2015-09-01", "2014-09-01"),
                dates2 = c("9/01/2018", "09/01/2017", "9/1/2016", "9/1/2015"),
                dates3 = c("March 1, 2019", "May 1, 2018", "January 20, 2017", "February 4, 2020"))
```

---
`r chunk_reveal("parse", break_type = "rotate", float = "none", widths = c(12, 1), title = "# Parsing Dates")`

```{r parse, include = FALSE}
dates
dates %>% mutate(dates1_parsed = ymd(dates1)) #ROTATE
dates %>% mutate(dates2_parsed = mdy(dates2)) #ROTATE
dates %>% mutate(dates3_parsed = parse_date(dates3, format = "%B %d, %Y")) #ROTATE
```

---
# Time is Weird

- Leap days and leap seconds mean that physical time is not the same as calendar time
  * lubridate `durations` represent physical time
  * lubridate `periods` represent the passage of calendar time

```{r}
time_length(mdy("05-27-2022")-mdy("05-27-1983"), "years")
time_length(as.period(interval(mdy("05-27-1983"), mdy("05-27-2022"))), "years")
time_length(as.period(interval(mdy("05-27-1983"), mdy("05-28-2022"))), "years")
```

---
`r chunk_reveal("age", break_type = "auto", float = "none", widths = c(12, 1), title = "# Age math")`

```{r age, include = FALSE}
birth_date <- ymd("2001-09-01", "2000-09-01")
test_date <- ymd("2020-09-01", "2019-09-01")
(test_date-birth_date)/365.25
as.period(interval(start = birth_date, end = test_date), unit = "years")
test_date - years(1) + days(7)
```
---
`r chunk_reveal("tz", break_type = "auto", widths = c(2, 1), title = "# Time Zones")`

```{r tz, include = FALSE}
t1 <- as_datetime("2022-01-27 10:39:28", tz = "America/Los_Angeles")
t1
tz(t1)
t2 <- as_datetime("2022-01-27 13:39:28", tz = "America/New_York")
t2-t1
t3 <- as_datetime("2021-10-15 10:39:28", tz = "America/Los_Angeles")
t3
t4 <- as_datetime(now())
t4
as.period(interval(start = t1, end = t4), unit = "days")
with_tz(t4, "America/New_York")
force_tz(t4, "America/New_York")
```

---
# Factors Represent Categories
```{r}
x <- c(1, 1, 2, 3, 1, 4)
x <- factor(x, levels = c(1,2,3), labels = c("rarely", "neutral", "frequently"))
x
```
- levels restrict the possible set of values

- levels are ordered, which carries forward to output, modeling, graphics, etc.

- factors work as dummy codes; use as.numeric(factor) to treat as a continuous variable in models
---

`r chunk_reveal("factors", break_type = "auto", widths = c(1, 1), title = "# Factors")`

```{r factors, include = FALSE}
ds <- starwars
unique(ds$eye_color)
ds <- ds %>% mutate(eye_f = factor(eye_color))
fct_count(ds$eye_f, sort = T) %>% slice_head(n = 5)
fct_count(ds$eye_f, prop = T) %>% slice_head(n = 5)
```

---
`r chunk_reveal("releveling", break_type = "rotate", float = "none", widths = c(8, 1), title = "# Setting factor levels")`

```{r releveling, include = FALSE}
ds <- ds %>% select(name, eye_f)
ds #ROTATE
ds %>% mutate(eye_f2 = factor(eye_f, levels = c("blue", "brown"))) #ROTATE
ds %>% mutate(eye_f2 = factor(eye_f, levels = c("blue", "brown"), labels = c("bl","br"))) #ROTATE
ds %>% mutate(eye_f2 = fct_lump(eye_f, n = 3)) #ROTATE
ds %>% mutate(eye_type = fct_collapse(eye_f, human = c("blue", "brown"), nonhuman = c("yellow", "red"))) #ROTATE
```

---
`r chunk_reveal("reordering", break_type = "rotate", float = "none", widths = c(8, 1), title = "# Reordering factor levels")`

```{r reordering, include = FALSE}
fct_count(ds$eye_f) #ROTATE
fct_count(fct_rev(ds$eye_f)) #ROTATE
fct_count(fct_infreq(ds$eye_f)) #ROTATE
fct_count(factor(ds$eye_f, levels = c("red", "brown", "blue"))) #ROTATE
```

# Part 2: Tidying Data
---
# Why do data need to be wrangled and tidied?

- Data files are often created without the foresight of how they might be used by computers
  * Instead, they are made to look nice for humans

- We need to tidy data to make it convenient for programming
  * Format is dictated by analyses
  * You may need multiple formats
---
# Tidy Data (Wickham, 2014)

- Each variable is a column
  * Variable: “All values that measure the same underlying attribute”
- Each observation is a row
  * Observation: Unit for which all variables were measured (person, session, trial, etc.)
- Each type of observational unit is a table
  * e.g., participant questionnaire vs trial-by-trial data
---
`r chunk_reveal("selectcols", break_type = "rotate", float = "none", widths = c(8, 1), title = "# Dataset Preparations")`
```{r selectcols, include = FALSE}
print(relig_income, n = 5)
relig_income %>% select(religion, contains("$")) #ROTATE
relig_income %>% select(religion, starts_with("$")) #ROTATE
relig_income %>% select(religion, contains("k")) #ROTATE
relig_income %>% select(religion, starts_with("$"), ends_with("k")) #ROTATE
```
---
class: inverse, center, middle
# Dataset Transformations 
---

`r chunk_reveal("pivot-longer", break_type = "auto", widths = c(2, 1), title = "# Multiple Columns -> One Variable ")`
 
```{r pivot-longer, include = FALSE}
ds <- read_csv('data_cleaned/vocab_annoying_headers.csv') %>% 
  mutate(id = "Jonah", dob = as.Date("2017-08-30"), .before = "age_12")
ds %>% print(n = 25) 
ds %>% pivot_longer(-(id:dob), names_to = "age", values_to = "word") 
ds %>% pivot_longer(-(id:dob), names_to = "age", 
                    names_prefix = "age_", values_to = "word")
ds %>% pivot_longer(-(id:dob), names_to = "age", 
                    values_to = "word", 
                    values_drop_na = T, names_prefix = "age_")
```
---

`r chunk_reveal("pivot-wider", break_type = "auto", widths = c(2, 1), title = "# One Column -> Multiple variables")`
 
```{r pivot-wider, include = FALSE}
ds <- read_delim(list.files(path = "data_headers", full.names = T),
                 col_names = c("field", "value"), col_types = c("cc"), 
                 delim = " ", n_max = 8, id = "filename")
print(ds)

ds <- ds %>% pivot_wider(id_cols = "filename", 
                         names_from = "field", 
                         values_from = "value")
ds
```
---
`r chunk_reveal("separate", break_type = "auto", widths = c(2, 1), title = "# One Variable -> Multiple Variables")`
```{r separate, include = FALSE}
ds 
ds %>% separate_wider_delim(filename, 
delim = "/", names = c("dir", "file"))
```

---
`r chunk_reveal("unite", break_type = "auto", widths = c(2, 1), title = "# Multiple Variables -> One Variable")`
```{r unite, include = FALSE}
ds 
ds %>% unite(col = "block_speed_condition", 
Block, speed, condition, sep = "_")
```

-unite()
---

`r chunk_reveal("bindcols", break_type = "auto", widths = c(2, 1), title = "# Binding Columns")`
 
```{r bindcols, include = FALSE}
star_wars_numeric <- starwars %>% select(where(is.numeric)) #87x3
star_wars_numeric
star_wars_char <- starwars %>% select(where(is.character)) #87x8
star_wars_char
star_wars_combined <- bind_cols(star_wars_numeric, star_wars_char) #87x11
star_wars_combined
```
---
`r chunk_reveal("bindrows", break_type = "auto", widths = c(2, 1), title = "# Binding Rows")`
 
```{r bindrows, include = FALSE}
s1 <- starwars %>% slice_sample(n = 2) #2x14
s1
s2 <- starwars %>% slice_sample(n = 2) #2x14
s2
s3 <- starwars %>% slice_sample(n = 2) #2x14
s3
star_wars_combined <- bind_rows(s1, s2, s3) #6x14
star_wars_combined
```
---

`r chunk_reveal("join", break_type = "auto", widths = c(2, 1), title = "# Joining Data")`
 
```{r join, include = FALSE}
fnames <- list.files(path = "data_headers", full.names = T)
header <- read_delim(fnames, col_names = c("field", "value"), col_types = c("cc"), delim = " ", n_max = 7, id = "filename") %>% pivot_wider(id_cols = "filename", names_from = "field", values_from = "value")
trials <- read_tsv(fnames, col_names = c("trial_num", "speed_actual", "speed_resp", "correct"), skip = 8, id = "filename")
header 
trials 
left_join(header, trials, by = "filename") 
left_join(slice_sample(header, n = 5), trials, by = "filename") 
left_join(slice_sample(trials, n = 5), header, by = "filename") 
```
